optionsReviewed: Original plus three alternatives per row. No fifth option is present in the current comparison.
status: Selection only; scene assets have not been replaced.

wall.name: Dirty leaking concrete wall
wall.reason: Use the same stained concrete treatment throughout. Fit wall sections to the existing footprints; carry this concrete tone onto retained bunker modules.

floor.name: Hangar Concrete Floor
floor.reason: Use one scuffed gray concrete material across slabs. Add local grime and impact decals for variation, with consistent texture scale.

stair.name: Keep original stair
stair.reason: Keep the individual steel treads and existing climb geometry. Match their finish to the selected dark industrial grates; the alternatives are whole stair assemblies.

rubble.name: Rubble Pile - Photoscan (Optimized)
rubble.reason: The gray concrete debris belongs to the same damaged bunker. Reduce mesh cost for repeated piles and vary rotation rather than mixing different rubble styles.

truck.name: Crashed Abandoned Truck - Game Ready
truck.reason: The damaged military-green pickup fits the scavenged battlefield and has a manageable mesh count. Desaturate paint and match the environment dust.

barrel.name: Barrel Pack - Low Poly Props
barrel.reason: Choose muted olive and gray variants from this single pack; reserve its red variant for explosive barrels so color communicates gameplay.

bunker.name: Keep original bunker
bunker.reason: Keep the modular bunker shell and its layout. Match its surface to the selected stained wall concrete; none of the complete-building alternatives replaces this module cleanly.

container.name: Freight shipping container - Rusted
container.reason: Use the same rusted freight model for all three containers. Preserve the red, blue and gray identities with equally faded paint and the same rust treatment.

ramp.name: Keep original ramp
ramp.reason: Keep the full-width walking slope. The alternatives are narrow vehicle rails or folding ramps; finish the current mesh in the same worn steel as the stairs.

tunnel.name: Keep original tunnel
tunnel.reason: Keep the rectangular concrete service passage and unify its material with the bunker. Subway tubes and bridge girders would change the architecture.

column.name: Keep original column
column.reason: Keep the square structural supports, using the same stained concrete as the walls. The alternatives add decorative bases, round damage or complete support assemblies.

supply.name: Cargo Crate
supply.reason: The olive cargo case reads as practical military storage. Reuse this one case family with small stencil variations; keep hardware dull and dust consistent.

sandbags.name: Sandbags
sandbags.reason: This stacked, weathered bag model matches the human defenses. Reuse its bag scale and faded canvas tone at every barricade.

generator.name: PE-77-D Generator
generator.reason: The olive PE-77-D has the right utilitarian military design. Match its worn paint to supply crates; retain dark steel fittings.

spool.name: Cable Spool
spool.reason: A simple wooden cable drum fits the same grounded industrial setting and stays light enough for repeated props.

bunk.name: Military bed
bunk.reason: The worn military cot fits an improvised bunker barracks. Keep faded canvas close to the sandbag palette and retain the low cover height.

trader.name: Abandoned Sci-Fi Control Console
trader.reason: The abandoned control console feels assembled from real industrial equipment. Use a restrained amber or green screen and faded military paint.

door.name: Metal door bunker
door.reason: The plain heavy steel door fits concrete service rooms and carries convincing wear. Resize to each opening and use one dark, desaturated metal finish.

gate.name: Game-Ready Roller Shutters
gate.reason: This simple gray shutter suits the existing vertical motion and matches the plain industrial doors. Keep the existing red warning strip. Its listing is CC BY-SA; retain that attribution/license information.

hazard.name: Floor Grate Small Pack [Free]
hazard.reason: Use one grate set for every hazard slot, in the same dark steel as stairs. Keep steam and electricity as runtime effects and use red only for active warnings.

flank.name: Worn concrete wall
flank.reason: A worn concrete panel keeps the breakable route in the same material family as the walls. Divide it into the existing fracture pieces during integration.

tube.name: Weathered Fluorescent Light/Lamp
tube.reason: Use the lightweight version of this weathered fluorescent housing for all tube fixtures, with one cool-white emission color.

emergency.name: Abandoned Factory Warning Light
emergency.reason: The caged factory warning lamps fit the same aged electrical hardware. Use restrained red emission only while the alarm is active.

work.name: Game Ready - Floodlight
work.reason: This practical twin-head construction light suits the bunker work areas. Retint the stand to faded olive and use the same cool-white bulbs as the tube fixtures.

pipe.name: Modular Pipes
pipe.reason: Use one modular pipe family for consistent pipe diameters, fittings and wear. Bring the brass-looking finish toward oxidized steel with localized brown rust.

cable.name: Modular cables 1m
cable.reason: Use this single cable system in matte charcoal. Follow the existing cable routes and keep connectors at a consistent scale.

scout.name: Terminator T-600
scout.reason: The actual T-600 preserves the older, heavier machine identity. Bring its metal into the same worn gunmetal palette as the T-800. This is a source for optimization: the listed 698k-triangle mesh needs LODs and rigging before use.

endo.name: TERMINATOR: T-800 Endo-Skeleton (Damaged)
endo.reason: This damaged T-800 is the shared body choice for Endo and Heavy. Its listed 8,244 triangles suit waves better than the much denser alternatives. Use dark worn steel, polished edges and small red eyes; validate the supplied rig and provenance.

heavy.name: Shared T-800 body + Heavy loadout
heavy.reason: Reuse the selected damaged T-800 body from the Endo row, then add the existing Heavy weapon and armor. Sharing the skull, limbs and materials makes this read as the same machine series. The noncommercial T-800 listing and unrelated combat robots are weaker production choices.

t1000.name: T1000 (T2)
t1000.reason: Choose the complete, relatively light T2 humanoid. Give it a continuous smooth chrome surface with far less grime than the mechanical units: its liquid-alloy identity should remain distinct.

hkaerial.name: Hunter Killer Tank and Aerial
hkaerial.reason: Use the aerial from this shared HK set, with the same gunmetal, vents and red optics as its tank companion. Separate the two vehicles before integration.

hktank.name: Hunter Killer Tank and Aerial
hktank.reason: Use the tank from the same HK set as the aerial. The shared proportions and detailing make a more coherent Skynet fleet than mixing creators and vehicle styles.

soldier.name: Sci-Fi Soldier / Futuristic Combat Trooper
soldier.reason: This comparatively light tactical soldier has the right silhouette. Use faded olive and charcoal cloth, remove faction markings and bright visor emission, and add restrained Resistance markings.
